slice: exploring: humpback song between societies; migration as co-chaining and bi-tunneling

items.sentence: Between selves, a same-existing-society co-chains unrelationing two-way, each self pacing its own time and abundancing in no self alone.
items.text: Humpback whales of the east Australian coast sing a song; in one season 2 of 82 singers are singing a new song nearly the same as the west Australian whales' song, the next season most of 112 singers are singing the old or the new and three a song mixing both, and in under two years the new song alone is sounding. Across six Pacific populations over a decade, songs pass almost always eastward, once westward, from the east Australian population toward French Polynesia over about two years, a new song typically becoming dominant within one breeding season; most songs blend the past year's material with new material, occasionally a completely new song, and how songs pass between populations, by a few males moving or by whales hearing songs while swimming together on migration, is a suspicion still to observe.

Migration is geodesic parity co-chaining and bi-tunneling: co-chaining along, a route and a song going on through generations and seasons, each young self opening with its elders' going as its prior; and bi-tunneling across, a flock's leaders and followers sharing thermals within one going, and a song passing between whole societies across an ocean, one social moral competency along and across.
